summary.text: Randall Gauvin is the Republican candidate for Maine House of Representatives District 75 in the November 3, 2026 general election, and he was the Republican nominee for the seat in 2024.
On his campaign website he describes a career in emergency medicine in Farmington, ending with his retirement in 2020.

paragraphs.text: Gauvin writes on his campaign website that he was born and grew up in Aroostook County, was educated at the University of Maine and Duke University, and moved to Farmington in 1976 with his wife.

He worked in emergency medicine in Farmington throughout his career, first as a first responder and paramedic and then as a physician assistant in the emergency room at Franklin Memorial Hospital, and retired in 2020.

He says he has since helped organize and work at the St. Joseph Center Food Pantry, serves on the board of the Care and Share Food Closet in Farmington, belongs to the Rotary Club of Farmington, and has been elected to the Farmington Board of Selectmen.
In the 2024 general election for District 75, Gauvin lost to Democrat Stephan Bunker, 2,317 votes to 2,310.
He advanced from the Republican primary on June 9, 2026, with 728 votes in the first round.
His campaign website lists fiscal responsibility, health care accessibility, hunger, the economy, citizens' right to protect themselves, and parental rights among his priorities.
